degree_requirement.value: first professionally qualifying degree in the field of “Informatik” or Computer Science or in a related study program
degree_requirement.quote: The specific admission requirement is a first professionally qualifying degree in the field of “Informatik” or Computer Science or in a related study program.

value.area: Foundations of computer science in total (the three areas below)
Theoretical Computer Science (formal languages, automata, computability, complexity, logic; discrete structures/mathematics, algorithms, data structures and digital logic do not count)
Additional computer science, not including the thesis

subject_credits.quote:
In the last application periods, less than 5 % of applicants fulfilled the entry requirements listed below and could be admitted. Therefore please read the following list thoroughly and please inform yourself about the contents of the different fields of study. In particular, the field of Theoretical Computer Science was not covered in most applications. Theoretical Computer Science includes courses i.e. on the topics formal languages, automata, computability, complexity, logic. Courses on discrete structures, discrete mathematics, algorithms, data structures, digital logic, design and analysis of algorithms are not recognized in the field of Theoretical Computer Science .

► Study programs in the above subject area and related study programs must contain at least the following components:

- 36 CP in foundations of computer sciences, including 12 CP in the field of Theoretical Computer Science , 12 CP in the field of Computer Engineering or Information Technology, 12 CP in the field of Methodological and Practical Computer Science

- 18 CP in the field of Mathematics,

- and additionally, at least 30 CP in the field of computer sciences, not including your thesis

value.min_score: higher B2 (certificates from the Faculty IV list)
overall band 6.5 (5.5 is not enough even if the certificate states B2)

value.test: University degree from a 'native English' country (Antigua & Barbuda, Australia, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Cook Islands, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Ireland, Jamaica, Canada, New Zealand, Philippines, Saint Kitts & Nevis, Saint Vincent, Singapore, Trinidad & Tobago, United Kingdom, United States); English-taught degrees from other countries are not accepted

english.quote:
Please note that a higher B2 English level is required. For the IELTS test, an overall band score of 6.5 is required, even if an overall band score of 5.5 confirms a B2 on the certificate.

- I studied in Germany or abroad and my study program was offered in English. Will this be recognized as proof of English proficiency for the Master's program? A successfully completed degree at a university will only be recognized as proof of English proficiency if it meets our definition of “native English.” This currently applies to the following countries: Antigua & Barbuda, Australia, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Cook Islands, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Ireland, Jamaica, Canada, New Zealand, Philippines, Saint Kitts & Nevis, Saint Vincent, Singapore, Trinidad & Tobago, United Kingdom (Great Britain and Northern Ireland), United States of America.

work_experience.quote: You are not formally required to do an internship either before or during the program, but we recommend you do so.

application_route.quote:
Master’s applicants who earned or will earn their first university degree (generally a bachelor’s) at a German university and are applying with a ECTS certificate (European Credit Transfer System (ECTS), see infobox) must submit their application directly to the TU Berlin.

### First Degree Semester: Graduates who studied at a foreign university (primary university degree)

Applicants who completed their primary university degree (such as Bachelor’s/undergraduate degree) from a foreign university (EU or non-EU) or who are currently studying at a foreign university and want to apply with an ECTS certificate (see infobox) will need a preliminary review documentation (VPD) for their application to TU Berlin from the summer semester of 2026 onwards. This must be requested from uni-assist specifically for TU Berlin.

selection_process.quote: The Master's program is admission-free (open admission).

required_documents.quote: If your application has not been reviewed by the examination board in terms of content, it is highly likely that your application did not include one or more of the following documents: •    A recognized English language certificate (this is mandatory for all Master's programs) or •    A Suitability Assessment Form (this is mandatory for the Master's programs in Automotive Systems, Computer Science (Informatik) and Medientechnik).

language_of_instruction.quote: The master’s program is taught in English.
